title: Semiquavers
summary: Fit four quick notes into one beat and tap the patterns they make.

hook.text: Hummingbird wings. A drum roll. A buzzing bee. *Flight of the Bumblebee* is a famous piece that sounds like one, because its notes come so fast. Press play and tap your foot. Where does this tune start to buzz?

explore.text: Your turn. Count 1, 2, 3, 4 with the clicks. Tap once on every click. Then twice on every click: "run-ning". Then go faster still: four taps on every click, like "wa-ter-mel-on".
explore.goal: Tap along with all 4 [[bar|bars]]: one tap, two taps, then four taps to a click.

cards.text: One [[semiquaver|semiquaver]] lasts a quarter of a beat. It has a filled-in head and a stem with two hooks. Four [[semiquaver|semiquavers]] fit into 1 beat: say "wa-ter-mel-on" in one step.
[[semiquaver|Semiquavers]] in one beat are joined by two beams. Count them 1-e-and-a, 2-e-and-a: say the number on the beat, then "e", "and", "a" for the three quick notes after it.

One [[quaver|quaver]] and two [[semiquaver|semiquavers]] also fill 1 beat, in either order. Say "pine-ap-ple" when the [[quaver|quaver]] comes first. Say "ap-ple-pie" when the [[semiquaver|semiquavers]] come first.

alternative.text: Every hook halves the note. A [[crotchet|crotchet]] has none and fills 1 beat alone. [[quaver|Quavers]] have one hook and come 2 to a beat. [[semiquaver|Semiquavers]] have two hooks and come 4 to a beat. Count the notes in each beat: 1, 2, 4.

questions.prompt: Match each symbol with how long it lasts.
questions.hint: Every hook halves the length. A [[crotchet|crotchet]] is 1 beat, so each note with more hooks is half of the one before.

questions.prompt: Both clips tick at the same speed. Which one squeezes four notes into a beat?
questions.hint: Tap a steady beat while you listen. Which clip fits four notes between your taps?

options.reason: Clip B has two notes in each quick beat, so those are [[quaver|quavers]]. The four-in-a-beat [[semiquaver|semiquavers]] are in clip A.

questions.prompt: How many short notes last as long as one long note?
questions.hint: Work out how long each note lasts in beats: [[crotchet|crotchet]] 1, [[quaver|quaver]] ½, [[semiquaver|semiquaver]] ¼.

questions.prompt: This [[bar|bar]] is a tiny bit short. Add **one** note to fill it.
questions.hint: Three [[semiquaver|semiquavers]] make ¾ of a beat. How much is missing from the last beat?

questions.prompt: Listen, then tap this rhythm. One tap for each note, so four taps in each beat of [[semiquaver|semiquavers]].
questions.hint: Say "wa-ter-mel-on" for each group of four [[semiquaver|semiquavers]]: one tap on each syllable, all inside 1 beat.

questions.prompt: Tap this rhythm. One tap for each note.
questions.hint: Four [[semiquaver|semiquavers]] share 1 beat: tap on the click, then three more times before the next click.

questions.prompt: Tap this rhythm. Watch how each beat is filled.
questions.hint: Beat 1 is "pine-ap-ple" and beat 2 is "ap-ple-pie". After that, tap once on each of beats 3 and 4.

questions.prompt: Which note lasts the length asked?
questions.hint: The [[semiquaver|semiquaver]] has two hooks. It is the shortest note you know.

questions.hint: Work out how many beats the long note lasts, then how many beats each short note lasts.

questions.hint: Check each beat of quick notes: four [[semiquaver|semiquavers]] fill a beat.

questions.prompt: Match each symbol with how long it lasts.
questions.hint: Work out the shortest first: a [[semiquaver|semiquaver]] is ¼ beat, and each longer note is bigger than the one before.
A [[semiquaver|semiquaver]] lasts ¼ beat. How many quarters make a whole beat?

options.reason: Two notes in a beat are [[quaver|quavers]], which last ½ beat each. A [[semiquaver|semiquaver]] lasts only ¼ beat, so 4 fit.
Eight [[semiquaver|semiquavers]] fill 2 beats, not 1. Each lasts ¼ beat, so 4 of them make 1 beat.

points: A [[semiquaver|semiquaver]] has a filled-in head and a stem with two hooks. It lasts a quarter of a beat, so 4 fit into 1 beat.
Count four [[semiquaver|semiquavers]] as 1-e-and-a. In one beat they are joined by two beams.
One [[quaver|quaver]] and two [[semiquaver|semiquavers]] also fill 1 beat, in either order: "pine-ap-ple" or "ap-ple-pie".
